_synthetic: Synthetic. The ONE plan-week index and the week documents every Plan test reads: W45 to W52 of a made-up season plus the 2030-W11 mirror of the big fixture's week (the current week). Named so it sorts after contract.json, which the merge would otherwise let override it; the stream files hold no plan-week paths.

planned_done.vs_prev: Against week 45: 4 h 26 and 12.3 km. Less time, more running, because of the races.

went_well: Everything planned was done. The doubles came in 6 minutes inside its goal.
held_back: The singles ran 8 minutes over goal. Two red nights. Resting heart rate is still raised: 55 (Garmin), 60 (WHOOP).

next_week.summary: Recovery week: four classes, 3 hours firm. Three changes proposed.

report.story: Two races in four days is a lot, and the week shows it. The singles on Wednesday came in over goal, which is normal when the legs are still carrying Monday and Tuesday. Three days later the doubles went better than planned, with a steadier first half. Garmin's readiness fell to its lowest on the last morning, and WHOOP's recovery had two red nights in the second half. Everything planned was done, so the next days are about letting both numbers come back before any hard work.

insights.title: Why the singles was slow
insights.text: The first half was run at the doubles pace you had planned for Saturday. That cost the second half.

insights.title: What the red nights have in common
insights.text: Both followed an evening race or class that ended less than three hours before bed.
